From Latin vice (“in place of”), ablative form of vicis. Compare French fois (“time”) and Spanish vez (“time, turn”).

senses.d: Bad or immoral behaviour. (Especially often, a habit that harms oneself or others)
ex: Pride is a vice, not a virtue.
Smoking was a vice Sally picked up in high school.

senses.d: Any of various crimes related (depending on jurisdiction) to weapons, prostitution, pornography, gambling, alcohol, tobacco, or drugs.
A defect in the temper or behaviour of a horse, such as to make the animal dangerous, to injure its health, or to diminish its usefulness.
A tool for drawing lead into cames, or flat grooved rods, for casements.
A winding or spiral staircase.
A grip or grasp.
ex: Fang. If I but fiſt him once: if he come but within my Vice.

senses.d: in place of; subordinate to; designating a person below another in rank
ex: vice president
vice admiral

senses.d: Instead of; in place of; versus.
ex: He was gardener and out-door man, vice Upton, resigned.
A very small cab-boy, vice Stoopid retired, swung on behind Foker's vehicle; knock-kneed and in the tightest leather breeches.

senses.d: One who acts in place of a superior.

Proto-Indo-European *weyk-der. Latin victima Middle French victimebor. English victim From Middle French victime, from Latin victima (“sacrificial animal”). Although this root and victor drive from homophonous PIE roots, they are traditionally reconstructed as separate words and thus not cognates.

senses.d: One that is harmed—killed, injured, subjected to oppression, deceit, or otherwise adversely affected—by someone or something, especially another person or event, force, or condition; in particular
ex: The victim of the robbery gave a detailed statement.
crime victim

senses.d: One who is harmed or killed by a crime or scam.
ex: victims of assault; the murderer's victims
became another victim of the latest scam

senses.d: One who is harmed or killed by an accident or illness.
ex: a fundraiser for victims of AIDS; a victim of a car crash

senses.d: One who is harmed or killed as a result of other people's biases, emotions or incompetence, or their own.
ex: a victim of his own pride; a victim of her own incompetence

senses.d: One who is harmed or killed as a result of a natural or man-made disaster or impersonal condition.
ex: relief efforts to help victims of the hurricane
victim of an optical illusion; victim of a string of bad luck

senses.d: A living being which is slain and offered as a sacrifice, usually in a religious rite.
